title: A Saturday at the Market
subtitle: A weekly routine at the farmers market — and why it is about more than the shopping.
description: An A2 reading and listening text about a weekly trip to the farmers market, with food vocabulary, present-simple practice and comprehension exercises.
passage: Every Saturday, I go to the farmers market with my friend Grace. It is always busy and full of people. We like to go early in the morning, because it is not too hot yet and the best things are still there.

First, we look at the vegetables. There are so many colors: red tomatoes, green peppers, yellow corn. Grace loves to cook, so she buys a lot of these. She always says that good food starts with good ingredients.
Next, we go to the fruit stands. There are apples, bananas, peaches and strawberries. I love strawberries, so I always buy a small box. They are sweet and fresh, and they are perfect for breakfast.
After the fruit and vegetables, we walk to the meat and fish counter. There is chicken, beef and fish. Fish is my favorite. It is good for you, and I like to grill it for dinner.
We also stop at the bread stand. Fresh bread smells wonderful. We buy a loaf to eat with butter and jam. It is simple, but it is delicious.

The market is not only about food. There are clothes too, and sometimes there is live music. It makes the shopping fun. We see people we know, we say hello, and we talk for a few minutes. It feels like a community.
Before we leave, we get a cup of coffee. It is nice to sit down after walking around for two hours. We talk about our week, our plans, and what we are going to cook with everything we bought.
Going to the market is more than shopping. It is about enjoying the morning, seeing friends and trying something new. It is one of my favorite parts of the week.

vocabulary.definition: a small open shop at a market
recently picked or made; not old
the different foods you use to cook a dish
one whole piece of bread, before you cut it
to cook over direct heat, often outside
the long flat surface in a store where you are served
to visit a place for a short time

exercises.title: Understanding the Text
exercises.instructions: The questions use different words from the text. Think about the meaning, not the exact wording.

items.prompt: How often do they go to the market?
Why do the two friends get to the market early?
options: Because they prefer cooler weather and there is more product availability
Because the stands charge less before the crowds arrive
Because parking near the market is easier at that hour
items.explanation: “It is not too hot yet and the best things are still there” — cooler air, and the good produce has not been picked over.

items.prompt: Which of the two friends is the keener cook?
items.explanation: Grace “loves to cook” and buys a lot of vegetables; the writer only grills fish.

items.prompt: Why does the writer buy strawberries every week?
options: They like them, and eat them at breakfast
items.explanation: “I love strawberries… they are perfect for breakfast.”

items.prompt: What does the writer say is healthy?
items.explanation: Of the fish: “It is good for you.”

items.prompt: They sit down at the end. Why?
options: They are waiting for a friend
They are tired after walking for two hours
items.explanation: “It is nice to sit down after walking around for two hours.”

items.prompt: Why does the writer say the market “feels like a community”?
options: Because they meet people they know and stop to talk
items.explanation: The reason given is the people: “We see people we know, we say hello, and we talk for a few minutes.”

exercises.title: True or False?
exercises.instructions: Decide whether each sentence is true. The words are not the same as in the text.

items.statement: They shop before it gets hot.
items.explanation: True — they go early “because it is not too hot yet”.

items.statement: You can only buy food at this market.
items.explanation: False — there are clothes, and sometimes live music.

items.statement: They buy bread that has not been sliced.
items.explanation: True — a loaf is a whole, uncut piece of bread.

items.statement: The writer thinks where food comes from does not matter.
items.explanation: False — Grace's line, “good food starts with good ingredients”, says the opposite.

items.statement: The whole trip takes them a few minutes.
items.explanation: False — they walk around for about two hours before sitting down.

exercises.title: Market Words
exercises.instructions: Choose the word that fits each sentence.

items.prompt: The tomatoes are very ___ — they picked them this morning.
items.explanation: Fresh means recently picked or made.

items.prompt: We buy a ___ of bread every week.
items.explanation: Bread comes in a loaf. Strawberries come in a box, and coffee in a cup.
Ingredients are the foods you use to cook a dish.

items.prompt: I like to ___ fish for dinner in the summer.
items.explanation: To grill is to cook over direct heat.

items.prompt: We always ___ by the bread stand on our way out.
items.explanation: To stop by a place is to visit it for a short time.

discussion: Is there a market near you? What can you buy there, and how often do you go?
Do you prefer a market or a supermarket? Give two reasons.
Describe your own Saturday morning routine, using 'always', 'usually' and 'sometimes'.
Write a short paragraph (about 60 words) about a place near your home where people meet and talk.
